title_en: Supreme People's Court Releases Five Typical Cases of Drug-Related Crimes
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Releases Five Typical Cases of Drug-Related Crimes

Case 1

Huang Guoyun — robbery case

(1) Basic Facts

The defendant, Huang Guoyun, male, Han ethnicity, born on March 19, 1979, was a farmer.

At approximately 9:00 a.m. on March 7, 2008, the defendant Huang Guoyun, suffering from a drug craving and lacking money to purchase narcotics, entered the home of the victim, Deng Keneng (male, died at age 76), under the pretext of using the restroom. After Huang Guoyun's request for a loan was refused, he produced a fruit knife he was carrying and threatened Deng to hand over money. When Deng refused, Huang Guoyun slashed Deng's neck with the knife, causing a laceration of the right common carotid artery and jugular vein, resulting in hemorrhagic shock and death. Deng's wife, Huang Zhaozhao (victim, died at age 72), came upon hearing the noise. Huang Guoyun dragged Huang Zhaozhao into the second-floor bathroom and slashed her neck, causing a laceration of the left common carotid artery and jugular vein, resulting in hemorrhagic shock and death. Huang Guoyun seized approximately RMB 350 in cash and a wallet, among other items, before fleeing the scene.

During the second instance trial, the defendant Huang Guoyun reported certain clues relating to a robbery committed by fellow inmate Peng Yin, which were verified upon investigation.

(2) Judgment

The court held that the defendant Huang Guoyun, with the purpose of illegal possession, forcibly took property from others by violent means, and his conduct constituted the crime of robbery. Huang Guoyun, suffering a drug craving and needing money to purchase narcotics, entered the victims' home to borrow money and, upon refusal, used a knife to kill, resulting in the deaths of two persons. The means of the crime were brutal, the circumstances were particularly heinous, and the consequences and the crime were extremely serious, warranting punishment according to law. Although Huang Guoyun's reporting of some crime clues of another person, verified upon investigation, constituted meritorious performance, his crime was so extremely serious that it was insufficient for a mitigated sentence. Accordingly, a sentence of death was imposed and approved for the defendant Huang Guoyun for the crime of robbery.

Case 2

Li Ning — intentional homicide case

(1) Basic Facts

The defendant, Li Ning, male, Han ethnicity, born on September 23, 1983, was a farmer.

On the evening of July 7, 2009, the defendant Li Ning drove in an abnormal manner after ingesting narcotics. That same evening, Li Ning's friend, Tang Hao (victim, male, died at age 31), and others drove over to pick up Li Ning. At approximately 1:30 a.m. the next day, the vehicle in which they were traveling crashed onto a greenbelt and came to a stop after hitting a tree. Li Ning got out of the vehicle and beat Tang Hao before retrieving a single-edged knife from the vehicle and stabbing, slashing, and cutting Tang Hao dozens of times on the head, chest, abdomen, and waist, causing Tang Hao to die from craniocerebral injury combined with hemorrhagic shock. Li Ning then used a knife to stop a car and drove off, subsequently crashing onto a greenbelt and overturning. When he attempted to flee again, he was apprehended.

(2) Judgment

The court held that the defendant Li Ning intentionally and unlawfully deprived another of their life, and his conduct constituted the crime of intentional homicide. Li Ning, after ingesting narcotics, used a knife to perpetrate violence, killing one person, and later used a knife to stop a vehicle in order to flee the scene. The means of the crime were brutal, the circumstances were heinous, and the crime posed great social harm and was extremely serious, warranting punishment according to law. Accordingly, a sentence of death was imposed and approved for the defendant Li Ning for the crime of intentional homicide.

Case 3

Huang Chuanhui — intentional homicide case

(1) Basic Facts

The defendant, Huang Chuanhui, male, Han ethnicity, born on January 19, 1987, was unemployed.

At approximately 3:00 p.m. on August 1, 2009, the defendant Huang Chuanhui ingested a "magic mushroom" pill and subsequently experienced reactions including vomiting and impaired consciousness. He was taken by friends to a hotel room to rest. At approximately 1:00 a.m. the next day, when Huang Chuanhui brought his pregnant wife, He Qun (victim, died at age 24), to the room to rest, he conceived the idea of killing his wife. Using both hands, he violently choked He Qun's neck before taking out a dagger he was carrying and slashing and stabbing He Qun more than 20 times on the neck, back, and other areas, causing He Qun to die at the scene. Huang Chuanhui, carrying the knife, attempted to flee the scene but was caught by bystanders in the hotel lobby.

After the incident, the defendant Huang Chuanhui confessed and expressed remorse. The victim's family members indicated their understanding of Huang Chuanhui and requested a lenient sentence.

(2) Judgment

The court held that the defendant Huang Chuanhui intentionally and unlawfully deprived another of their life, and his conduct constituted the crime of intentional homicide. Huang Chuanhui, after ingesting narcotics, intentionally killed his pregnant wife by brutal means, making the crime serious. Based on the crime, a death sentence should have been imposed. However, considering that the incident occurred within a family setting, differing from intentional homicide crimes committed in society that severely threaten public security, and that Huang Chuanhui had a good attitude of confession after his arrest, obtained the understanding of the victim's family, and their economic losses were compensated according to law, a death sentence was imposed but with a two-year suspension of execution. Accordingly, for the crime of intentional homicide, the defendant Huang Chuanhui was sentenced to death, with a two-year suspension of execution.

Case 4

Fu Chengjun — endangering public security by dangerous means case

(1) Basic Facts

The defendant, Fu Chengjun, male, Han ethnicity, born on December 26, 1986, was an insurance company salesman.

At approximately 8:30 p.m. on May 26, 2010, the defendant Fu Chengjun drove a red "Besturn" sedan from his residence to pick up a friend. En route, Fu Chengjun stopped the vehicle and, inside the car, ingested the narcotic ketamine he had with him, before continuing to drive. When approaching a supermarket, Fu Chengjun experienced mild dizziness and excitement but continued driving. At approximately 8:50 p.m., after Fu Chengjun stopped the car (without turning off the engine), he experienced severe disorientation, severe dizziness, and hallucinations. Fu Chengjun then pressed the accelerator and drove forward, first lightly colliding with two tricycles. After a brief pause, he again pressed the accelerator and drove forward, colliding head-on with a moving tricycle, knocking down the tricycle rider and several pedestrians to the ground, and trapping the tricycle under the left front of his car. After stopping for about five minutes, Fu Chengjun again pressed the accelerator violently and drove forward, pushing the tricycle ahead of him, toppling numerous roadside stalls and knocking down multiple stall owners and pedestrians, until the wheels became stuck at a step and the car came to a forced stop. Fu Chengjun's driving rampage resulted in injuries to 20 persons, including one with serious injuries, four with minor injuries, and fifteen with slight injuries, and caused property losses totaling over RMB 16,000. After Fu Chengjun was apprehended, police recovered 2.33 grams of ketamine from the car he had been driving.

After the incident, the defendant Fu Chengjun confessed and expressed remorse. His family members reached settlement agreements with 25 victims.

(2) Judgment

The court held that the defendant Fu Chengjun, after ingesting narcotics and experiencing hallucinations, drove a motor vehicle in a densely populated area and caused an accident, then continued to ram into others, causing injuries to multiple persons and property damage. His conduct constituted the crime of endangering public security by dangerous means and should be punished according to law. Given that Fu Chengjun had a good attitude of confession after his arrest and obtained the understanding of the victims, whose economic losses were compensated according to law, a lenient punishment could be imposed at the court's discretion. Accordingly, for the crime of endangering public security by dangerous means, the defendant Fu Chengjun was sentenced to five years of fixed-term imprisonment.

Case 5

Zhang, Tian, Zhao, and Wang — drug trafficking case (juvenile crime)

(1) Basic Facts

Defendant Zhang, female, Han ethnicity, born on May 17, 1993, was unemployed.

Defendant Tian, female, Han ethnicity, born on January 2, 1995, was unemployed.

Defendant Zhao, male, Han ethnicity, born on December 30, 1992, was unemployed.

Defendant Wang, male, Han ethnicity, born on November 13, 1993, was unemployed.

In July 2010, on two separate occasions, Defendant Zhang sold a total of 30 grams of methamphetamine to Gu Taogen (separately prosecuted) downstairs at her temporary residence. On the early morning of July 21 of the same month, Zhang was caught at the scene while attempting to sell 73.9 grams of methamphetamine to Gu Taogen. Subsequently, police recovered 93.3 grams of methamphetamine and 8.8 grams of caffeine from Zhang's temporary residence.

In July of the same year, on two separate occasions, Defendant Tian sold a total of 10 grams of methamphetamine to Li Changlin at her temporary residence. The second occasion involved jointly selling 5 grams of methamphetamine with Defendant Wang. On July 19 of the same month, police recovered 2.7 grams of methamphetamine from Tian's person. After her arrest, Tian assisted the police in apprehending other criminal suspects.

In July of the same year, Defendant Zhao, at Li Changlin's request, sold 0.3 grams of methamphetamine to Xu Cheng and handed over the RMB 300 received to Li Changlin. In the early morning of July 17 of the same month, Zhao was caught at the scene while accompanying Li Changlin in a vehicle to sell 7.5 grams of methamphetamine. Police recovered 1 gram of methamphetamine from Zhao's person, and, based on Zhao's confession, recovered an additional 6.5 grams of methamphetamine from the vehicle.

(2) Judgment

The court held that Defendants Zhang, Tian, Zhao, and Wang, all knowing that methamphetamine and caffeine were narcotics, sold them, and their conduct constituted the crime of drug trafficking. Among them, Zhang trafficked a large quantity of drugs, Tian trafficked a relatively large quantity of drugs, and Zhao and Wang trafficked a small quantity of drugs, all warranting punishment according to law. Given that Tian was between the ages of 14 and 15 at the time of the crime and had demonstrated meritorious service by assisting the police in apprehending other criminal suspects after her arrest, and that Zhang, Zhao, and Wang were between the ages of 16 and 17 at the time of the crime, all were eligible for a lenient or mitigated punishment according to law. Furthermore, relevant evidence indicated that all four defendants had dropped out of junior high school and migrated for work, engaged in drug crime due to bad associations and drug use, and, after arrest, exhibited a good attitude of confession and voluntarily pleaded guilty at trial, allowing for a discretionary mitigated punishment. Considering the specific circumstances of each person's crime, Zhang, Tian, and Zhao were given reduced sentences, while Wang received a lenient sentence. Accordingly, for the crime of drug trafficking, Defendant Zhang was sentenced to nine years of fixed-term imprisonment; Defendant Tian was sentenced to three years and three months of fixed-term imprisonment; Defendant Zhao was sentenced to two years and four months of fixed-term imprisonment; and Defendant Wang was sentenced to one year of fixed-term imprisonment, suspended for one year and six months.
